cars.specification_market: V10 GT MF5 described in David Vivian’s 25 February 2009 evo firsthand drive. Reference year dates this report, not a verified chassis build or exact introduction. Twelve attributes retain its reported engine and drivetrain. No torque peak: the article differs between 6200 rpm and 6100 rpm. No timed acceleration: body says 0–62 mph while table says 0–60. Weight, power-to-weight, brake material and introduction date omitted; exact model debut conflicts with manufacturer retrospective. Manufacturer MF5 page also describes later twin-turbo power and automatic transmission; these are not V10 specifications. MF4 history establishes a larger, new-chassis programme relative to the MF3. Conservatively group MF4/MF5 road engines, bodies, reference years and upgrades once. No MF4-CS racer, prototype, modern Project Gecko/Thunderball or extra roadster count. Photo is a supplied-title MF5 coupe family illustration only, not authenticated as this test car, engine, exact year, chassis or original equipment.
cars.summary: The Wiesmann GT MF5 combines a front-mid-mounted BMW M V10 with a focused specialist sports-GT chassis and distinctive retro body. David Vivian’s period firsthand drive documents its driver involvement and chassis capability. It represents Wiesmann’s flagship performance-coupe programme, beyond rarity alone. Group the related MF4/MF5 road bodies and engine versions once; the earlier MF3 roadster is a different programme.
